q: How can a self-help group work out the carbon footprint of its products?
title: Carbon footprint for SHG products
short: Keep it simple and record-based. Note the fuel, electricity and main materials used for a batch, divide by the units made, and apply standard factors. A buyer or support agency can help with factors; the group's job is accurate records of what went into each batch.
audience: Self-help groups and the agencies that support them

ul: Date and products made, with count or weight.

p: Multiply each quantity by its factor, add them, and divide by units made. Keep the records so the figure can be checked.

senseible: Senseible reads supplier invoices into dated records with the quantity, unit and factor on each line, and marks lines without a usable quantity as needing data instead of guessing.
